A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgentExpt framework, corpus and recommendation tasks. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendix A.1–A.9, whose additions can be distinguished from relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original corpus analyses, baseline and dataset recommendation results in Table 2, and component ablations in Tables 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds comparator results, GPT-4o reranking comparisons, latency measurements and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The description-plus-citation-context retriever, diagonal/in-batch loss, top-three interaction-chain evidence and supervised reranker remain unchanged. The new prompts document existing components rather than establish a redesigned algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the corpus of 108,825 papers from ten AI venues during 2015–2025 for baseline and dataset recommendation. The appendix experiments retain these tasks and coverage; no additional benchmark, domain or distinct input scenario is established.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the five original comparators and adds DataHunter and DataFinder to both recommendation tasks. Table A.6 additionally evaluates BM25 plus GPT-4o and the AgentExpt retriever plus an unfine-tuned GPT-4o reranker, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols include GPT-4o retriever/reranker combinations and average per-query timing on one A800 GPU. A.5 also describes pool/global-inventory selectivity despite retaining precision labels. The chronological 8:1:1 split is newly disclosed, not an established revision to a previously specified split.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds tests of whether a general GPT-4o reranker compensates for BM25 retrieval or replaces the specialized reranker; A.3 adds an accuracy–latency analysis. These extend the original component ablations substantially. The interaction-chain results in A.5 largely relocate and elaborate v1 Figure 2 rather than constitute a new experiment.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty. Appendix A.4 newly reports five independent runs with different seeds, means and standard deviations, and paired t-tests against SymTax, including p < 0.01 and p < 0.001 markers. An increase from an earlier run count cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Original Table 2 scores and Tables 3–5 remain unchanged, but v2 adds comparator, reranking, latency and significance results. For example, Table A.6 reports baseline HR@10 of 0.5427 for BM25 plus GPT-4o and 0.6501 for AgentExpt retrieval plus GPT-4o; A.7 reports 0.367-second AgentExpt latency versus 0.692 for SymTax. The prose also corrects ablation decline percentages and the reuse-rate threshold from 90% to 85%.

T1.justification: The formal task, loss and interaction-chain equations remain equivalent, with no new proofs. However, A.5 introduces a different mathematical quantity in prose: retrieved-pool size relative to the global inventory, rather than v1 Figure 2's overlap precision within the candidate pool. Figure A.6 inconsistently retains the precision labeling.

C1.justification: v2 removes the explicit claims of the first large-scale recommendation dataset and approximately 85% coverage from the abstract/contributions. The corpus, collective-perception retrieval, chain-guided reranking and headline performance claims remain. The conclusion additionally frames AgentExpt as infrastructure for auditable automated experimental choices.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning AI-venue coverage, literature cutoffs, incremental updates and popularity bias, recommending decision support rather than prescriptive use. The appendix adds interpretations about retrieval ceilings, specialized training and interactive latency. Its reinterpretation of the retained precision percentages as inventory compactness introduces ambiguity.

D1.justification: v1 references an appendix that is absent from the supplied PDF. v2 documents chronological 8:1:1 splitting and supplies four operational prompts for query summaries, collective perception, entity filtering and reasoning generation. Reported training hardware changes from two A100 GPUs to two A800 GPUs. These are substantial documentation additions without establishing a method redesign.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning through dataset-bias and benchmark literature, including Torralba and Efros, Paullada and colleagues, and Ott and colleagues, plus reasoning-recommendation and latency/usability references. Several general web-agent references disappear. The three principal related-work categories and the central distinction from prior recommendation systems remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around context-dependent experimental suitability. Related work is condensed, method exposition and results discussion are streamlined, and the conclusion is expanded. Dedicated limitations, impact statements and an organized appendix substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different template and typography. Figure 1 gains a solution overview; v1 Figure 2 is split between v2 Figure 5 and Figure A.6; the reuse plot is redrawn and relabeled. Table 2 expands, three appendix tables are added, and four prompts receive boxed displays.

improvement.justification: The disclosed split, operational prompts, uncertainty reporting and substantive limitations make v2 easier to assess and reproduce. Broader comparisons and supplementary analyses also help, but their reporting has problems: DataFinder duplicates all HAtten scores in Table 2 without explanation, and A.5 conflates precision with inventory proportions. These issues temper the gains, leaving a clear but limited overall improvement in transparency and presentation.
